concept: Finished deck shipping storage and reorder economics

claims.text: PrintNinja’s help page contains inconsistent shipping estimates: its card-specific answer gives 6–8 weeks shipping after 3–4 weeks printing, while its general answer gives five weeks standard ocean shipping. Preserve both attributed estimates and confirm a project schedule. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Panda says it includes spare components for customer replacement requests. This is a manufacturer support provision, not a measured transit damage rate. Replacement stock and reshipment expenses need separate project assumptions. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

In its historical account of 2021 conditions, Pandasaurus describes smaller print batches as more flexible, but also reports restocks failing to arrive when needed. Use that experience to scope replenishment risk; it does not supply current lead times or a guaranteed reorder schedule. (low confidence)

PrintNinja says shipping costs vary with destination and residential versus commercial address type. Very large orders by volume or weight need a custom freight quote. US delivery scenarios therefore require actual addresses and package quantities. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Shopify’s reorder framework multiplies average sales rate by lead time and adds safety stock; its lead-time strategy includes manufacturing and supplier delivery. Apply consistent time units and project-specific demand rather than inventing a reorder threshold. (low confidence)

PrintNinja labels standard ocean delivery uncertain and recommends extra schedule allowance. Reorder planning should allow for replenishment delays instead of assuming advertised transit is guaranteed. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-10)

UPS calculates dimensional weight from parcel volume divided by a rate-specific divisor and rounds fractional dimensional pounds upward. The guide lists 139 for Daily Rates and 166 for Retail Rates. Confirm the applicable rate agreement and final outer-carton dimensions. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

UPS recommends a rigid shipping box and adequate cushioning. A game’s retail package therefore needs a separate transport-packaging decision; these guidelines do not establish a damage rate for this game. (low confidence)
PrintNinja’s card-game price table explicitly excludes shipping, sales tax and duties. Those production prices alone do not establish delivered cost. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-02)

PrintNinja’s customs page says its pricing for US deliveries includes customs, duties and taxes. This is a vendor statement about its delivered service, not evidence that imported card games universally have zero import costs. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20)

PrintNinja’s published card-price table excludes shipping, sales tax, and duties; its help page says US-address quotes include taxes and duties in USD. Confirm the actual delivered quote boundary before adding import costs again. These are vendor statements, not an independent tariff determination. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

PrintNinja offers partial expediting: some copies travel by air and the remainder by ocean. It also warns that shipping times are approximate outside its guaranteed expedited service; model a split shipment as an option requiring its own quote. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-10)

PrintNinja’s fulfillment page advertises storage at $0.08 per cubic foot per week. Treat this as its published affiliate rate, not a complete fulfillment price: the page separately calls for a custom shipping quote for diversion to EFS. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-04-27)

EFS says it imposes no surcharge or higher fee solely for long-term storage. It also says it does not insure clients’ stored inventory. Storage aging charges and inventory insurance therefore need separate checks in a warehouse comparison. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

For a comparison model, keep parcel volume, warehouse volume over time and destination-specific delivery as separate inputs: UPS prices dimensional space, PrintNinja publishes storage per cubic foot per week, and PrintNinja says address type affects shipping. This is a modeling recommendation, not a measured finished-game cost. (medium confidence)

A finished-game delivery model should separate manufacturing, receiving, handling, packaging, postage, and storage. PrintNinja excludes shipping from published manufacturing examples, while Laguna lists receiving, fulfillment, shipping boxes, postage, and storage separately. (medium confidence)

Panda says custom shipping cartons and palletizing/shrink-wrapping or floor loading are included, but door-to-door shipping is excluded from manufacturing prices. This describes a manufacturer service, not independently demonstrated shipping protection. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Laguna’s US card-game/tarot schedule lists receiving at $6 per box or $60 per pallet, fulfillment at $3.00–$3.50 per shipped box, and packaging boxes at $0.50–$1.50. Storage is $2–$10 per box/month or $20–$45 per pallet/month. Shipping is separate. Rates may change with fragility, dimensions, and quantity; this schedule is not a quote for the worked game. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Inventory carrying costs include capital opportunity cost, insurance, handling, and deterioration as well as storage. PrintNinja also warns that self-fulfillment requires warehousing, order work, tracking, shipping, and customer service. Home storage and self-fulfillment therefore need explicit costs. (medium confidence)

Fanatics Collect warns that damp storage can warp cards, promote mold, and make cards stick together; excessive pressure can deform cards. This collector guidance identifies risks to evaluate for paper inventory, but supplies no finished-game warehouse specification or damage probability. (low confidence)

PrintNinja offers partial air expediting with the balance sent by ocean, and split delivery to multiple addresses. These are candidate ways to bridge an urgent need or divide warehouse and home stock; no project saving is quantified here. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-10)

PrintNinja offers FOB by custom quote with shipment from Shenzhen port onward arranged by the customer, or EXW with customer-arranged factory pickup and full shipping. Model these responsibilities separately from delivered US quotes; applicable self-import duties remain unresolved. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

A fulfillment provider’s Media Mail price menu does not establish that a party game qualifies. USPS describes games, including board games, as entertainment distinct from qualifying media. Establish postal eligibility for the actual product before using the menu’s media rate. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2018-07-01)
